note: City of La Plata campground on its 81-acre city reservoir 2.5 miles east of town: a gravel loop of pads in open grass on the slope above the east shore, with picnic tables and fire pits, plus a playground, picnic pavilion and an 18-hole disc golf course. The city posts no camping fee; call City Hall. --Claude
summary: City page confirms 30 sites (20 new + 10 original) with electric/water, dump station, FCFS 'NO reservations'; no fee, season or amperage posted anywhere on the city site; MDC lake page confirms the 30 sites, but MDC's map (11/6/2018) doesn't show the campground. Lakeview held (~100-130 m over open grass). Phone matches.
flags: FEES: not posted. The city's Park & Recreation page (browser-rendered) gives location, the 30 sites, hookups, dump station, FCFS, and 'For questions call La Plata City Hall 660-332-7166 Monday thru Friday 8 am - 4 pm' - no rate. The city's Reservations, Ordinances and Forms & Permits pages render empty resource lists (no fee schedule or ordinance online). MDC's lake page names only the city's boat fee ('$2.00 per day or $25.00 per year for those using boats on the lake'). A web search found only Campendium (user-reported '$10 fee for dry camping', last nightly rate $20 reported September 2024), which isn't citable; fees left unset and the note keeps 'call City Hall'.
SEASON: no season stated by the city or MDC; left unset.
HOOKUPS: electric is stated but no amperage, so hookups.electric stays absent; water confirmed.

MDC: the La Plata City Lake area page says 'This Area is owned and Maintained by: City of La Plata ... The City provides 30 camping sites, a playground, and a picnic pavilion. For more information or to report problems, please contact: City of La Plata 660-332-7166.' The MDC map (Last Updated 11/6/2018) legend has parking, privy, picnic area, fishing dock and boat ramp but no camping symbol, and MDC GIS layer 27 has no camping point - MDC's map does not show the campground.

WATERFRONT (lakeview, held): the camping loop (about 45 x 160 m, rows of pads with tables, on open grass) sits about 100-130 m east of the nearest open water, across an open meadow with scattered shrubs and a reed/tree fringe at the shore; the 81-acre lake is in plain sight. Not on-water: the meadow, mowed trails and the loop road lie between.
